title: Garbage Collection Makes Rust Easier to Use: A Randomized Controlled Trial of the Bronze Garbage Collector
venue: ICSE ’22 (44th International Conference on Software Engineering)
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether adding an optional garbage-collection abstraction to Rust can make the language easier and more productive to use for novice programmers. The authors focus on a common pain point in Rust: ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, and aliasing, especially when implementing data structures that need multiple references or mutable aliases.

To test this, they designed Bronze, a library-based garbage collector for Rust with a GC reference type (GcRef<T>) that simplifies aliasing and mutable shared access. They ran a randomized controlled trial in a sophomore-level programming languages course, assigning students to either use Bronze or use traditional Rust across a multi-part programming assignment. The assignment moved from basic syntax to ownership/borrowing and then to a more difficult aliasing task involving parent-child links and caches.

The study involved students enrolled in a required programming course at one university in the United States. Quantitative outcomes included task completion and self-reported time; the authors also collected survey responses and free-text comments. Bronze improved completion and reduced time on the hardest aliasing task among those who finished it, but did not improve total time across the whole assignment because Bronze students later redid the aliasing task without GC. The paper concludes that GC can substantially reduce architectural and aliasing complexity for Rust newcomers, though learning Rust’s core ownership concepts remains necessary.

identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI / chatbot-style system that produces or adapts text and could be used for feedback or instructional support, without a specific named product identified in the paper.
identified_tools.use_case: Not studied in this paper. The paper is about the Bronze garbage collector for Rust, a programming-language usability intervention, not an AI tool.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an RCT, but it does not evaluate any AI tutoring, feedback, or generative tool. The intervention is a Rust garbage-collection library, so there is no AI-tool evidence to extract.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI system is studied, so there is no instructional or learning impact attributable to an AI tool. The reported effects concern programming-language usability, not teacher coaching or lesson feedback.
